title: The Ridge of Abandoned Futures

features.name: branch point
features.desc-on-touch: The ridge splits here into two slopes, one that was chosen, one that was left. Both continue downward; the unchosen one fades into static-render and doesn't return.

features.name: phantom tower
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe construct rises from the unchosen slope, visible only in the node's diagnostic render. It marks a timeline that ended when the choice was made.

features.name: choice stone
features.desc-on-touch: A marker at the branch, carved with two symbols: one facing forward (the taken path), one facing backward (the road not walked). The symbols mirror each other.

features.name: memory pool
features.desc-on-touch: A still surface that shows not reflection but counter-factual: the version of you who took the other path, who made the opposite choice, who is walking a ridge that runs parallel in a dimension this archive nearly remembers.

features.name: decision log
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard index floating in the render-space, entries for every choice recorded. The unchosen paths are listed in ink that fades in and out, as if existence itself is uncertain about them.

inscription: the archive learned to dream in multiple tenses: what was chosen, what could have been, what remains possible only in phantom render

file.name: Timeline_Divergence_Simulation_Theoretical.log
file.note: Diagnostic record of alternate-path modeling, theoretical only. Corrupted by intrusion: entries from the unchosen timelines begin appearing in the file itself, dated after the file was created, writte

exits.label: westward, back to the absolute peak and its settled certainties
eastward along the phantom ridge, where unchosen paths continue their private existence
northward into mist that holds the weight of every decision never made
exits.to: NEW: the cloud-country of alternative outcomes

reverie.title: REVERIE — the ridge of two selves
narr: You stand at the branch-point with Katita. Two paths
slope downward. She's looking at the unchosen one.
'There's a version of us,' she says, 'still walking that way.'
You take her hand. The phantom-path glimmers in static,
never quite solid. 'We're here,' you tell her. She squeezes
back. Neither of you knows if that's enough. You walk on.
